title: prefetch-experimentation-governance-and-dashboard-contract-2026
author: Priya Chandran
content:
Overview
-------
This document defines the governance, metric contract, dashboard requirements, alerting thresholds, and operator runbook for prefetch experiments and production rollouts at Redwood. It covers how to author, validate, monitor, and retire prefetch cohorts so experiments produce reliable SLO signals and operators have a clear playbook for triage and rollback.

Goals
- Make prefetch experiments observable and reversible with clear, testable metric contracts.
- Minimize operator cognitive load for prefetch-induced degradations.
- Balance cost savings from prefetch with latency and quality SLOs.

Scope
- Applies to any prefetching layer that influences LLM inference runtime (edge hints, KV prefix warmers, proactive KV fanout).
- Includes staged experiments (canary → regional cohort → global) and on-call procedures.
- Excludes model architecture changes; those follow model-onboarding flow.

Roles and ownership
- Experiment Owner: Product / ML Engineer who declares hypothesis and defines cohorts.
- Observability Owner: Platform Dashboarding team (eng-platform dashboards) responsible for dashboard delivery and alerting rules.
- Operator Owner: Platform Operators / Oncall SRE team who perform triage and rollback.
- Reviewer(s): Runtime & Serving team for safety and resource contention review.

Metric contract (required for any prefetch experiment)
- Must be signed off by Experiment Owner and Observability Owner before activation.
- Contract fields (minimal):
  1. primary_latency_metric: e.g., p95_request_latency_ms (end-to-end request path).
  2. secondary_cost_metric: e.g., prefetch_token_cost_per_minute (billing reconciled metric).
  3. quality_guardrail: e.g., percentage of generation completions with hallucination_score > 0.6 (from quality-evals) or model-quality-regression-alert_count.
  4. resource_contention_metric: e.g., gpu_utilization_by_pool, preemptible_eviction_rate.
  5. experiment_buckets: JSON array string with cohort names and fraction (e.g., [{\"name\":\"canary\",\"fraction\":0.01},{\"name\":\"region-A\",\"fraction\":0.2}]).

Minimum acceptance criteria before canary promotion
1. p95_request_latency change <= +10% absolute and latency delta < 50ms (whichever is smaller).
2. quality_guardrail regression <= 0.5% (absolute).
3. prefetch_token_cost increase <= 12% for targeted traffic slice, with projected global cost delta within finance guardrails.
4. gpu_utilization increase controllable: sustained increase < 6% above baseline for the same window.

Dashboard requirements (deliverables by Observability Owner)
- All prefetch experiments must provide a dedicated dashboard named: Prefetch / <experiment-name> / <region>.
- Required panels (minimum):
  * Traffic split timeline (cohort fractions over time).
  * p50 / p90 / p95 request latency per cohort (end-to-end).
  * Token throughput and token cost per cohort.
  * Model quality signal (eval-set coverage and guardrail metrics) per cohort.
  * Resource metrics: GPU utilization, host load, eviction rate.
  * Error budget burn and SLO delta per cohort.
  * Canary health heatmap (binary health per metric & cohort).

Example dashboard panel specifications (table)
| Panel | Query (PromQL / explained) | Refresh | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---|
| p95 end-to-end latency (cohort) | histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{cohort=~\".*\"}[5m])) by (le,cohort)) | 15s | observability-team |
| Prefetch token cost (cohort) | increase(prefetch_tokens_total{cohort=~\".*\"}[1m]) * token_cost_per_unit | 60s | finance-observability |
| GPU eviction rate | rate(gpu_evictions_total[5m]) | 30s | runtime-team |

Alerting and severity mapping
- Priority levels (P0, P1, P2) define operator cadence and escalation.
- Baseline alert rules must be created alongside the dashboard.

Alert rule table:
| Rule name | Trigger | Severity | Initial action | Escalation after |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| prefetch-p95-degradation | p95(cohort) > baseline_p95 * 1.10 AND delta_absolute > 30ms for 5m | P1 | Pager to oncall + open incident channel | 15m escalate to runtime lead |
| prefetch-quality-regression | quality_guardrail regression > 0.5% over baseline within 30m | P0 | Immediate pager to oncall & model owner, auto-hold rollout | 5m escalate to Head of Applied ML |
| prefetch-cost-surprise | prefetch_token_cost / expected_cost > 1.3 for 30m | P2 | Slack alert to finance+owner | 60m notify billing |

Operator runbook (step-by-step)
1. Acknowledge alert and open incident channel using incident template \"prefetch-experiment-alert\".
2. Immediately check the Prefetch / <experiment> dashboard and cohort traffic split panel. Confirm that traffic fraction aligns with rollout plan.
3. Validate primary signals: latency p95, quality, GPU utilization, eviction rate. Capture one-minute and thirty-minute deltas.
4. If quality regression or p95 breach meets P0/P1 criteria, execute fast rollback: run the rollout control-plane command to set cohort fraction to 0 for the offending cohort. Example CLI:
   - rdxctl rollout set --experiment <name> --cohort <cohort> --fraction 0 --reason \"auto-rollback: quality/latency breach\"
5. After rollback, monitor stabilization for 30 minutes. If stabilization fails, escalate to runtime lead and begin deeper diagnostics (see \"Deep diagnostics\" below).
6. For cost-only alerts (P2), pause further rollout and run cost-query to compute projected monthly delta. If projected delta exceeds finance cap, throttle rollout to a maximum aggregate fraction specified in the experiment contract.

Deep diagnostics checklist
- Correlate latency increases with cache-miss rates and KV prefix hit ratios.
- Inspect model-variant fallback logs (look for increased fallback_count per request).
- Check for correlated infra events: node reboots, driver errors, preemption spikes.
- If GPU memory churn is high, check for KV cache growth per-tenant; consider reducing warmset sizes.
- Run a targeted replay of 1000 representative requests from canary cohort in the lab environment to reproduce latency/quality regression.

Post-incident retro and requirement updates (process)
1. Owner must file a short incident summary within 24 hrs: what happened, how we detected, rollback actions taken, immediate mitigations.
2. Within 5 business days, schedule a retro with Observability & Runtime to: review metric contract fidelity, update dashboard panels/queries, and adjust acceptance criteria.
3. Update the experiment’s metric contract and dashboard spec in the experiment README and mark the contract version (semver) that rolled back.

Retrospective template (required fields)
- Title, incident-id, experiment-name, cohort, time-window, action-taken, root-cause-hypothesis, evidence (links to traces, logs, queries), follow-ups (owners + ETA).

Roadmap items (Q3–Q4 2026)
- Auto-scoped rollback: small controller to calculate delta vs contract and automate canary fraction adjustments (Q3 2026).
- Standardized prefetch cost model and tooling (cross-team finance + platform) to produce projected monthly deltas from short-term signals (Q4 2026).
- Prefetch lab harness: replayable, synthetic traffic generator to validate large-cohort behavior in a sandbox (Q4 2026).

Appendix A: Example PromQL and Grafana snippets
- p95 latency per cohort (5m window):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"inference\",cohort=~\".*\"}[5m])) by (le,cohort))
- prefetch token cost (1m):
  sum by (cohort)(increase(prefetch_tokens_total{cohort=~\".*\"}[1m])) * 0.00012  # token cost unit placeholder

Appendix B: Change checklist before enabling canary
1. Contract signed by Observability Owner and Runtime Lead.
2. Dashboard deployed and linked in experiment README.
3. Alert rules created in Paging stack with correct severity and runbook link.
4. Operator oncall notified of planned canary window via calendar invite.
5. Rollback command tested in staging.

Appendix C: Quick links
- Experiment template: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/prefetch-experiment-template
- Rollout CLI reference: internal://rdxctl-rollout-cli
- Incident template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-templates/prefetch-experiment-alert

Notes and caveats
- Do not authorize global rollouts that bypass the dashboarding requirement. Any experiment lacking the dashboard contract must be blocked.
- Quality guardrails must use the same evaluation dataset across cohorts when possible; if the experiment exercises a novel prompt set, add an explicit note and longer canary window.
